scenarios.name: update-type-overdraft-rate
scenarios.why: SELECT +0, valid type: UPDATE sets type, overdraft and rate; the COMMAREA refilled from the host variables, the dates reformatted from Db2's ISO text; 'Y'

scenarios.name: update-negative-balance-account
scenarios.why: a negative DECIMAL(12,2) balance into COMM-AVAIL-BAL / COMM-ACTUAL-BAL (S9(10)V99)

scenarios.name: update-max-values
scenarios.why: COMM-OVERDRAFT 99999999 into INTEGER, COMM-INT-RATE 9999.99 into DECIMAL(6,2) (the largest each PICTURE holds); balance 9999999999.99

scenarios.name: leap-day-opened
scenarios.why: an account opened 2024-02-29: the date's parts moved by position

scenarios.name: account-not-found
scenarios.why: SELECT INTO no row: SQLCODE +100, 'N', no UPDATE

scenarios.name: other-sort-code-not-found
scenarios.why: COMM-SCODE is overwritten by the program's own SORTCODE (987654): account 123456/00000001 is never read, 987654/00000001 is

scenarios.name: blank-account-type
scenarios.why: type all spaces: 'N' after the SELECT, no UPDATE

scenarios.name: type-starts-with-space
scenarios.why: type's first byte a space: 'N', no UPDATE

scenarios.name: null-statement-date
scenarios.why: ACCOUNT_LAST_STATEMENT is NULL and its host variable has no indicator: SELECT INTO is SQLCODE -305, 'N', no UPDATE

scenarios.name: mortgage-update
scenarios.why: a second successful update, a large negative balance

notes: CBSA's update-account service (UPDACC, LINKed with the UPDACC copybook's COMMAREA): the account is read by the program's own sort code (987654) and COMM-ACCNO with a SELECT INTO from Db2 table ACCOUNT (unqualified: the bind's QUALIFIER, IBMUSER); a failed SELECT (+100, -305 ...) or an account type that is blank or starts with a space gives COMM-SUCCESS 'N' and no UPDATE; otherwise ACCOUNT_TYPE, ACCOUNT_INTEREST_RATE and ACCOUNT_OVERDRAFT_LIMIT are UPDATEd, and the COMMAREA is refilled from the host variables, each date reformatted from Db2's character form (YYYY-MM-DD) to DDMMYYYY. The table is compared after every scenario.
